Why is there a movement for Flash to be abandoned and replaced with other, similar, systems?

One of the biggest reasons is safety.

<begin ELI5> Flash has a very bad history of bad people using it to take control of your computer. The people who make Flash constantly have to fix what lets the bad people do this- but it doesn't seem to stop them for long. Also, this doesn't look like it will get better soon- so the smarter people who work with computers around the world are telling people to not use flash wherever they can. HTML5 doesn't have the same problems. (Or at least nearly as much) <end ELI5>

Well, there's the issue of utilizing your GPU. HTML5 allows your computer to use it, and Flash doesn't. This means that your CPU must do everything when running Flash, inherently slowing down your machine more than necessary.

Then you have the problem of Flash only being optimized for Windows. When you try to run it on Unix (Linux) or FreeBSD (OSx/iOS), you end up with problems and performance issues. This is primarily because of the first point, but it is also a major issue all on its own.

HTML5 is touchscreen compatible, whereas Flash is not... I don't think I need to go into this any more than that.

While HTML5 isn't completely open-source, it is when compared to Flash. Flash is nearly completely closed, and controlled by Adobe Systems. This means that, instead of being able to run natively in your browser, you can only run Flash within a plugin downloaded from Adobe. HTML5 can run natively since it utilizes open-source components and doesn't require a plugin to run. If you can run HTML (which everything on the web has been coded in since the beginning of forever) you can run HTML5.

HTML5 doesn't support DRM, which is pretty self-explanatory. This, again, goes back to the last point of open-source components, but becomes a contentious point all on its own.

Then you can't forget all of the zero-day vulnerabilities that the Flash plugin has had lately. These are very important when regarding if you want to download it or not. And, without it, you can't use Flash.

Flash is like pandoras box, once you open it bad things can happen to your computer. Sure it's pretty and promises lots of content, but the good comes with the bad, and a lot of bad these days.

There is no reason to stick with flash. Html5 has greater potential and can pretty much "work everywhere" with some limitations like if someone was stupid enough to try to reach your website with internet explorer 5, in which case they should really take the hint and get a new operating system and a new browser.

tl;dr: Flash is painful to use. HTML5, much easier to use

Something that hasn't been brought up yet is that Flash is difficult to use. I've poked around with Flash- it sucks to write in. Adobe improved Flash creation with the programming language Flex. But after using Flex for awhile, it's firmly in my top two least favorite languages. It tries to bridge too many gaps in how programming languages work and ends up a muddled mess.

Incidentally, if any developers not familiar with Flex want details, let me know. I want to keep this explanation simple.

HTML5, on the other hand, is an extension of very familiar technologies- namely HTML and manipulating it through Javascript. Yes, you need to familiarize yourself with new tags, but it's all in a familiar context.

Ease of use gives you a few things. First, time to write and deploy new features is far shorter, increasing the amount of work a development team can do.

Easier to use means less likely to screw it up and far easier to find and fix problems.

Finally, it's easier to find people who can use that technology. Try hiring- or even finding- a Flex developer. Then try HTML5 developers.
